title: AI-Powered Browser Research & Reporting System
tagline: From a URL to a finished PowerPoint — automatically.
description: An end-to-end pipeline that drives a real browser to visit websites or platforms, extracts data, captures and crops screenshots, runs AI analysis on the collected material, and compiles structured insights into an automated PowerPoint report.
problem: Research and reporting work was done by hand: opening dozens of pages, copying information, taking screenshots, cropping them, pasting into slides and writing commentary. Slow, inconsistent, and impossible to repeat at scale.
solution: A Playwright-driven browser worker collects pages and screenshots, an image-processing step crops and normalises visuals, an LLM layer analyses the extracted content using structured outputs, and a report generator assembles everything into a branded PPTX deck — with a review step before delivery.

architecture.detail: List of target URLs / platform queries + report template
Playwright sessions with navigation, waits, scroll & capture
HTML → structured data; screenshots → cropped assets
LLM analysis with JSON-schema outputs per section
PPTX generation with slide templates + asset embedding

capabilities: AI analysis constrained to structured JSON outputs
Automated slide generation with images and commentary
Re-runnable: same input → consistent report structure
keyLearnings: Robust selectors and explicit waits matter more than speed in browser automation
Structured outputs make LLM results safe to drop into templates
Keep a human review step before reports leave the system

title: Intelligent SEO Research & Analysis Automation
tagline: A research system — not a ranking promise.
description: An automation and research system that analyses websites, surfaces technical issues, studies competitors, runs a keyword research workflow, captures evidence screenshots, and produces an AI-written analysis report. It supports SEO work; it does not guarantee rankings.
problem: SEO audits required manually crawling pages, checking technical signals, comparing competitors and compiling findings — repeated for every client with the same structure each time.
solution: A browser automation layer crawls the target and competitor sites, a checks module flags technical issues (meta, headings, links, performance hints), a keyword workflow organises research inputs, and an LLM layer turns raw findings into a structured, readable report with screenshots as evidence.
capabilities: Website analysis and technical issue identification
Keyword research workflow (inputs organised for human decisions)
keyLearnings: Rule-based checks + LLM explanation is more trustworthy than LLM-only audits
Research automation should present evidence, not conclusions presented as guarantees

title: Multi-Step AI Agent Workflow
tagline: Receive a task. Plan it. Use tools. Deliver.
description: A general-purpose agent loop that receives a task, analyses it, breaks it into steps, calls the right tools (browser, APIs, database, files), processes intermediate results, and produces a final output — with guardrails on tool use and step limits.
problem: One-shot LLM calls fail on tasks that need several actions, external data or verification. Each new workflow was being hand-wired from scratch.
solution: An orchestration layer with a planner → executor → reviewer loop. Tools are registered with typed schemas (including MCP servers), the agent picks and calls them step by step, and every run is logged so failures are inspectable.

architecture.detail: Planner / executor / reviewer loop with step limits
Typed tools + MCP servers (browser, HTTP, DB, files)
Run state, intermediate results, conversation context

capabilities: Typed tool calling with schema validation
Retry and fallback handling for failed steps
keyLearnings: Most agent failures are tool-contract failures — strict schemas fix more than better prompts
Step limits and explicit stop conditions keep agents predictable

title: Business Workflow Automation System
tagline: User input in. Decision, action and notification out.
description: A configurable automation system where user input is processed by AI, routed through API / browser / database tools, passed through decision logic, and turned into an output, report or notification.
problem: Teams were manually moving information between forms, spreadsheets, web portals and chat — error-prone, slow and invisible when something broke.
solution: An event-driven flow: inputs arrive via form, webhook or email; an AI step classifies and extracts structured fields; tools perform the required actions (API calls, browser tasks, DB writes); decision logic decides the next step; outputs go to reports, dashboards or notifications — with approval gates where needed.

architecture.detail: REST APIs, Playwright tasks, database writes

capabilities: Browser and API actions in one flow
keyLearnings: Idempotency and retries are essential for real business automations
Visible logs make automations trusted by non-technical teams
